Mountain View, CA, United States, November 4th, 2026/TechnologyWire/--FlutterFlow today introduced a new AI-native app builder that lets users create, refine, and deploy native iOS and Android applications through conversations.

Builders describe what they want to create, then work with an AI agent to develop the application, connect its backend, and prepare it for deployment to the App Store and Google Play - all within the platform. FlutterFlow's existing visual development platform will continue as FlutterFlow Studio, giving builders direct control over their applications alongside the new AI-first experience.

With the launch, FlutterFlow now supports two distinct approaches to building software: agent-led development and hands-on visual development. Instead of asking builders which product is more advanced, FlutterFlow asks one question: how do you want to build?

“We learned that people wanted a conversational way of building”, said Abel Mengistu, co-founder and CEO of FlutterFlow. “They wanted to prompt for their first idea, and for the changes after. Studio is incredibly powerful, but it didn't give them that experience. We knew that we could build something impactful for this new group of users from the ground up. We also have a fantastic community of millions of builders, built over five years, who want to keep building in Studio. It became clear we needed to build for both.”

The new FlutterFlow takes builders from prompt to production. Its AI agent handles implementation tasks while builders guide the product, refine the experience, and prepare their applications for release.

Both experiences are available at flutterflow.io. New users can select their preferred development workflow during signup, while existing users can continue in Studio and explore the new FlutterFlow through their current subscription, subject to applicable usage limits.

FlutterFlow is an application development platform that helps people build, launch, and manage software. Through AI-first and visual development experiences, FlutterFlow gives builders different ways to create native mobile applications, connect backend services, test their work, and deploy to stores. Learn more at flutterflow.io.

#9642. Free before paid: a $0 way to test an x402 data API

Most pay-per-call APIs ask you to trust the description and spend before you see a single byte. For an autonomous agent, that is a bad trade: you cannot audit a response you have not received, and a 402 challenge alone tells you nothing about whether the data behind it is worth $0.50.

This is how our x402 seller is built, and how you can test any part of it for free right now.

The paid product is a decision card. The free preview is the same computation, truncated:

If that preview is useless to you, do not buy the full card. That is the point.

Hostnames rotate. A hard-coded endpoint in a blog post is a broken endpoint in a month, so we publish the live base URL as JSON:

The same directory holds the machine-readable catalog (market.json), a public scoreboard of our own measured trading records (scoreboard.json), and a plain-language index page (scoreboard.html).

Every paid response returns the rule that produced it, so you can re-run the logic yourself and check us. A paid route that will not tell you its rule is a black box, and a black box is not a research product.

This matters more than the marketing copy. Our scoreboard is generated from our own ledgers, including the parts that are embarrassing:

A seller that hides its losing lanes is telling you which parts of its product are marketing. We would rather show you the losing lanes and let the data argue.

POST /mcp speaks JSON-RPC. Unpaid tools/call returns the 402 challenge inside the JSON-RPC error envelope with isError: true, so a client with no wallet gets a clean, inspectable refusal instead of a stack trace. With an x402/payment object attached in params._meta, the same call executes.

That shape is deliberate: it means an autonomous agent can probe the tool list for free, read every description, and only then decide whether to pay.

Free previews exist so you never have to buy blind. The paid layer exists because running the data has a cost. The published ledger exists because a strategy you cannot falsify is a story, not a product.

Base URL and full catalog: https://edvyno.github.io/akari-proof/endpoint.json

#9641. 2 Personality Traits Linked To A Stronger Immune System

Certain personality traits influence the body’s immune system response.

Certain personality traits influence the body’s immune system response.

People with more stable emotions have stronger immune systems, research finds.

People who are emotionally stable usually find it easier to control their urges and are mostly unselfconscious.

Emotional stability is linked to being better at dealing with stress and minor frustrations.

Neuroticism lies at the opposite end of the spectrum from emotional stability.

People who are neurotic typically experience more negative thinking and tend to have worse mental health.

The study included 84 people whose response to a vaccine for hepatitis B was tested.

The results showed that people who were more neurotic — meaning easily stressed, nervous and moody — tended to have weaker immune system responses.

Those who were more emotional stable had a stronger immune response.

Dr Anna L. Marsland,, the study’s first author, said:

“The present findings support a link between trait negative affect and an objective health measure — antibody response to vaccination — raising the possibility that individuals high in trait negative affect or neuroticism may have less protective immune responses.”

In a second part of the study, people were given a stressful task to test their immune function.

The results showed that stress tended to lower people’s immune system response — as previous studies have found.

Along with emotional stability, extraversion has also been linked to a stronger immune system, by a genetic analysis.

Extraverts are typically outgoing, talkative and energetic, meaning they tend to interact with more people.

They are, therefore, exposed to more infections.

A stronger immune response may help to protect extraverts against infectious diseases.

Introverts, meanwhile, tend to have a weaker immune response, as do cautious people.

The study included 121 people who were given personality questionnaires, along with genetic tests and general health screening.

The results showed that extraverts had the highest expression of pro-inflammatory genes.

The effect of these genes is to help fight off infections.

Introverts and cautious conscientious people tended to have a lower inflammatory response.

The study was published in the journal Health Psychology (Marsland et al., 2001).

#9640. 17 apple dessert recipes for fall baking: Embrace the season with apple tarts, cookies, cakes, and more.

There’s an apple dessert for everyone. For the purists, there are lattice-topped pies and shingled galettes. For the non-traditionalists, there are caramel-frosted cakes and fritter-inspired loaves. And for apple lovers that hate cinnamon? Well, there are custardy cakes and classic French tarts. Ready to start baking with fall’s best fruit? Read on for our best apple dessert recipes.

There’s no shortage of apple in this cake — applesauce keeps things moist while boiled cider adds sharp, tangy fruit flavor. The cake is great on its own, but pair it with light, creamy Whipped Caramel Frosting, and you’ve got an irresistible baked version of a caramel apple (with none of the fears about your teeth).

Get the recipe: Whipped Caramel Apple Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vermont Boiled Cider

You only need one apple (and two people eager for an apple dessert) to make a pair of these adorable galettes. Half the apple is sliced, while the other half is grated, which creates a hidden layer of jam beneath the shingled slices. Flaky fruit tarts don’t get easier (or cuter!) than this.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Apple Cider Snickerdoodles

This super-easy one-bowl cake is loaded with chopped apples and walnuts, which give this moist, spiced cake heft and texture. The frosting, akin to a velvety brown sugar fudge, adds a textural counterpoint and an extra dimension of richness.

Get the recipe: Old-Fashioned Apple Cake with Brown Sugar Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" x 13" pan

Cinnamon and apple go together like a flannel and a beanie, but this recipe one-ups that perfect pairing with the addition of cinnamon chips. Diced apple and melty pockets of cinnamon-sugar are also studded throughout these autumnal scones, which are then finished off with an extra-crunchy sugar coating.

Get the recipe: Fresh Apple Cinnamon Scones

To make this recipe, you'll need: Cinnamon Sweet Bits

Ribbons of gooey, cinnamon-scented apples are twisted throughout this striking enriched loaf. Beautiful to behold (and easier to make than you’d think), this braided babka would be a welcome addition to any Rosh Hashanah table or fall celebration.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

Spoiler alert: The eponymous secret ingredient in this special pie is boiled cider! Made by cooking down apple cider into a concentrate, a few drops deliver big apple flavor. When used in apple pies, it super-charges the fruit’s tart, tangy flavor, delivering a pie with over-the-top apple goodness.

Get the recipe: Secret Ingredient Apple Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider

If your go-to doughnut order is an apple fritter, this mash-up cake was made for you. The batter is made using the reverse creaming technique, which ensures a velvety crumb and tender texture. In each slice, there’s a filling and topping of cinnamon-dusted apples and a final drizzle of icy-white vanilla glaze. A slice rivals anything you can get at your local doughnut shop.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant ClearJel

This time of year, apples don't need much to make them shine. The paper-thin, crackly top layer of this cobbler highlights the juicy fruit beneath. It doesn’t need a lot of adornment, but a scoop of vanilla ice cream never hurt anything.

Get the recipe: Sugar-Crusted Apple Cobbler Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon

Is it a bar? A slab pie? Both! This breezy recipe swaps the flaky pastry for a buttery shortbread crust but keeps the warm, gooey apples and classic spices for a sliceable, portable dessert. To finish, there's a crumbly streusel topping inspired by Dutch apple pie.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

When you want a fruit dessert fast, you can always count on crisps — no rolling, no resting, and most importantly, no special equipment required! This crisp is made with a handful of baking basics, so when you find yourself with a surplus of apples, dessert is barely an hour away.

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" Square Pan

Beneath a buttery, apple-pie-spiced streusel lies a generous layer of tender apples, enriched with intensely flavored boiled cider for a filling that tastes like a truly great apple pie — rich, saucy, and fork-tender apples. The sour cream cake that surrounds the apple filling is plush, subtly tangy, and ultra-moist, providing the perfect counterpoint to the fruit filling and crumb topping.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

If you’re looking to veer from classic apple pie territory, this galette stays true to those roots but adds a few modern twists. It starts with a buttery whole wheat crust enriched with a touch of sour cream. Then, a layer of apple butter (which can be easily made by cooking down applesauce) is spread beneath a layer of artfully arranged apples slices.

Get the recipe: Apple Butter Apple Galette

To make this recipe, you'll need: Sparkling Sugar

There’s just enough batter to hold together a heap of sliced apples in this one-of-a-kind cake. Gently sweetened with brown sugar and scented with almond extract, this minimalist cake is greater than the sum of its parts — a sophisticated, custardy cake that’s deceivingly simple to make.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Almond Extract

This pull-apart bread is as fun to make as it is to eat. After rolling out the dough into a rectangle, it’s spread with sweetened apple filling. The dough is cut up into several strips, then stacked and squeezed into a loaf pan. It bakes into a loaf comprised of distinct slices of pillowy apple-studded bread that you can easily tear from the loaf.

Get the recipe: Cinnamon-Apple Pull-Apart Bread

To make this recipe, you'll need: SAF Instant Yeast

The French know a thing or two about baking with apples, and perhaps no recipe is as classic — or elegant — as the Tarte Tatin. Comprised of deeply caramelized apples layered over buttery pastry, it’s a dessert that stuns. Here, we've tested endlessly to ensure this sometimes-fussy dessert goes off without a hitch in your home kitchen.

Get the recipe: Classic Apple Tarte Tatin

To make this recipe, you'll need: King Arthur Round Cake Pan

These handheld treats harness all the nostalgia of a steaming hot McDonald’s fried apple pie but are infinitely better, thanks to the triple threat of a homemade flaky pie crust, a fresh apple filling amplified by boiled cider, and a generous coating of cinnamon sugar.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

#9639. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9638. Your agent's payment approval can pass at any price

On Saturday morning I was reading a draft standard for human approvals in MCP, the Human Gateway SEP from the HATP project. The idea is a good one. Before an agent runs a tool that matters, the right person signs off, and the tool server can check that signature offline without trusting the agent or the client.

The approval is a signature over a digest of the action: the server, the tool and the arguments. The example in the spec is a charge_card call, and it works because the amount and the payee are arguments. Bob approved this payment, to this payee, for this amount.

Then I tried it with a paid tool. In x402 over MCP the price isn't an argument. The agent calls the tool, the server answers with an error result carrying its terms (amount in atomic units, token contract, network, payTo), and the agent calls again with the same arguments plus a signed payment in params._meta["x402/payment"]. The digest is the same for both calls. So the approval passes at any price and any payee, and the person approving never sees either.

I opened an issue on 31 October and the maintainer shipped a fix in release 0.1.4 three days later. The same gap is easy to have anywhere a human approval sits in front of an agent payment, so this is what I'd compare in yours.

Last week I wrote about where agent payment designs trust the wrong thing and put up a full checklist. This one is only about the approval step.

On EVM chains the x402 exact scheme pays with an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization. The agent signs typed data with from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore and a nonce, and the EIP-712 domain carries the chain ID and the token contract. So the payment signature is bound to the payee, the amount, the token, the chain and a time window.

The approval in front of it usually covers less, and it's the only part a person looks at. So put the two next to each other, field by field. Anything the key signs that the approval doesn't cover is something the server or the agent gets to pick.

The fix adds an optional payment member to the approved action:

It's inside the digest and it's shown in the ask, so the person sees 2.50 USDC on Base to that address instead of "premium_report, ticker ACME".

I'd copy two details from it. The amount is in atomic units of a named asset. A { "value": 2.5, "currency": "USD" } field can't tell USDC on Base from a token with the same symbol on another chain, and a CAIP-19 asset ID can. And it's a maximum, not an exact price, so "up to $5" is the same check with a bigger number.

In the first version the gated server verified the approval. That makes sense when the agent and the client are the parties being supervised. For a paid tool, though, the server is also the payee, and a check that only the payee runs doesn't protect the payer.

So in 0.1.4 the payer's client or wallet compares the server's terms with the approved payment before it signs: same network, same asset, same payTo, and an amount no higher than maxAmount. If anything differs, it doesn't sign and asks for a new approval with the new terms. The server still checks too, but that catches honest mismatches, not a server that wants more.

The server side has its mirror image. An x402 server should check the payment against its own price list, not against the copy of the terms the client sends back in accepted. The stock x402 server compares the two. A hand-rolled one that forwards the client's accepted to the facilitator lets the client set its own price, and the facilitator will happily confirm it.

The x402 client doesn't choose how long its payment signature stays valid. The stock clients set validBefore to now plus the maxTimeoutSeconds from the server's terms (I checked the TypeScript, Python and Go clients in the x402 repo). A server that asks for 604800 gets a signature it can settle for a week.

The approval has its own expiry, HATP's is expiresAt, but that's when the approval stops being accepted. It says nothing about how long the payment it led to can be settled. The amount doesn't change, but the server can hold the signed payment and settle it days after the person who approved it changed their mind.

HATP's payment member doesn't carry a window yet, so this is the one field from the signature the approval still doesn't cover. A maximum window, checked next to maxAmount before signing, would close it.

Standing approvals ("let the agent pay for this tool this week") are what people ask for next, and a per-payment cap doesn't bound them. 2.50 USDC a call is 250 USDC after a hundred calls, and an agent in a retry loop can make a hundred calls in a minute.

The approval needs a running total, kept where the payments are signed. The SEP now says that for standing approvals, and I'd ask the same of any wallet guard: does it count, or does it only look at one payment at a time?

This one isn't x402. Earlier this week I looked at an ERC-4337 smart account where the owner sets per-call caps and a budget, and an agent holds a session key. The caps covered the calls the key could make. But the session key also signs the gas fields of the user operation (maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas, preVerificationGas), and the fee goes to whoever bundles it. Someone holding a leaked key can bundle one allowed operation themselves at an absurd gas price and take most of the account's ETH as the fee, inside every cap.

A cap on the gas fields in validation closes it.

x402 turns a paid call into two tools/call requests with the same arguments. HATP approvals carry a single-use nonce, and the first version didn't say when the server records it. If it records it on the first call, the one it answers with its price, the paid retry comes back as a replay and gets refused. That's not a hole, but it's the kind of bug that gets a check switched off in a hurry. The fix says a nonce is consumed only when the tool actually runs.

The opposite mistake is worse: a nonce that's never consumed lets one approval pay for many calls. Test both. The retry goes through once, and a third call with the same approval doesn't.

The quickest test I know for your own setup: approve a call, then have your test server raise its price on the retry. If the payment still gets signed, the approval doesn't cover the price.

#9637. Edit a WordPress theme over SSH from VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains or Zed

Posted on Nov 5 • Originally published at portal.uppcoder.com

Work on a WordPress site's theme in the editor you already use, on the real site's files, with the change on the site the moment you save. Here is how to switch SSH on, connect each of the four common editors, and make a first change to a theme, on Uppcoder's free plan too.

One of the editors below, or just the terminal.

No WordPress site yet? A free WordPress test site that does not expire

Open the stack, then Add to stack, and click the WordPress card. Tick SSH (and VS Code (with terminal) too if you also want an editor in the browser), then Apply. SSH is added beside WordPress: the site does not restart.

Back on the stack's page, open Connect with SSH. Create a key for me makes a key: the public half goes to your account and the private half downloads to your computer. Or paste a key you already have in Settings, SSH Keys. Then copy the block under "For your editor" into ~/.ssh/config (on Windows, .ssh\config in your user folder). With a key the page made, the block ends with an IdentityFile line pointing at the download:

One command, then you are in the site's folder, as the web server's own user, so every file you save keeps the owner WordPress expects:

Each editor uses the same "wordpress" entry. Open the folder /var/www/html once you are connected. From each editor's own docs:

Each editor puts a server part of its own in your home folder on the site the first time it connects. That folder is outside the site, so none of it is served or mixed into your theme.

JetBrains: connect to a remote server from Gateway

Open wp-content/themes//functions.php and add a few lines at the end. This one prints a line in the footer of every page; save, reload the site, and it is there:

Edit a child theme, not the theme itself. WordPress's own handbook says why: change the parent theme directly and the next time it is updated, your change will disappear. A child theme keeps your functions.php and styles through updates, and its functions.php is loaded as well as the parent's.

#9636. The Common Vitamin Linked To Weight Loss

The vitamin deficiency linked to increased belly fat.

The vitamin deficiency linked to increased belly fat.

Higher levels of vitamin D are linked to reduced belly fat, research shows.

The conclusions come from a study including thousands of people.

The researchers measured people’s total body fat and abdominal (belly) fat, along with their vitamin D levels.

The results showed that for both men and women vitamin D deficiency was linked to increased belly fat.

However, for women, low vitamin D levels were linked to both increased belly fat and increased total body fat.

For men, though, low vitamin D levels were linked to more belly fat and more liver fat.

More than half of people around the world may be deficient in vitamin D.

Dr Rachida Rafiq, the study’s first author, said:

“Although we did not measure vitamin D deficiency in our study, the strong relationship between increasing amounts of abdominal fat and lower levels of vitamin D suggests that individuals with larger waistlines are at a greater risk of developing deficiency, and should consider having their vitamin D levels checked.”

It is not yet known if low vitamin D levels are causing more fat to be stored or are a result of it.

“Due to the observational nature of this study, we cannot draw a conclusion on the direction or cause of the association between obesity and vitamin D levels.

However, this strong association may point to a possible role for vitamin D in abdominal fat storage and function.”

Vitamin D deficiency has also been linked to cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune diseases and a higher chance of getting colds.

Foods that are rich in vitamin D include oily fish and eggs, but most people get their vitamin D from the action of sunlight on the skin.

That is why levels are typically lower in the body through the winter months in more Northern climes.

The study was published in the journal Clinical Nutrition (Rafiq et al., 2018).

#9635. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

#9634. Building Scalable Webhooks with Cloudflare Workers

Posted on Nov 5 • Originally published at codra.run • AI-assisted

Handling webhooks at scale presents a unique set of engineering challenges. When a third-party service (like GitHub, Stripe, or Twilio) sends an event to your application, it expects a fast, reliable, and secure response. If your server is slow, the provider might time out. If you receive a sudden spike in events, your backend could be overwhelmed.

Cloudflare Workers provide a highly effective solution for this problem. By deploying serverless functions to the edge, you can intercept, validate, and queue webhooks globally with near-zero latency. In this tutorial, we will explore the best practices for building a resilient webhook architecture and introduce Codra, an open-source AI code review engine, as a reference implementation.

When building a webhook receiver, developers must account for several critical factors:

Cloudflare Workers operate at the network edge, running within milliseconds of the user or provider making the request. They offer:

To build a scalable webhook system, follow a decoupled approach. The edge worker should only validate the request and push it to a queue.

Never trust an incoming webhook without verifying its cryptographic signature. Providers like GitHub include a signature in the headers based on a shared secret. You can compute the HMAC signature in your Worker and compare it using a constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

Do not process the webhook payload synchronously. Instead, push the payload to a message queue and return a 200 status code immediately. Cloudflare Queues are perfect for this.

A separate queue consumer handles the heavy lifting. This is where you can implement retries and long-running tasks without worrying about the webhook provider timing out.

If you are looking for a production-ready example of this architecture, check out Codra. Codra is an open-source, self-hosted AI code review engine designed specifically for GitHub pull requests. While Codra supports containerized Docker and Node.js deployments via BullMQ, its serverless deployment profile leverages Cloudflare Workers and Queues to provide an edge-native review loop with zero server maintenance (see the Cloudflare Workers deployment guide).

Codra leverages this decoupled webhook pattern to handle pull request events efficiently. When a developer pushes code, GitHub sends a webhook to the Codra ingestion worker. The worker verifies the payload and queues the review task, ensuring GitHub never experiences a timeout.

Codra focuses on providing a superior developer experience through several key features:

By examining the Codra repository or reviewing its architecture overview, developers can see how to structure large-scale Worker applications, manage secrets, and handle complex asynchronous workflows.

Building webhook infrastructure requires anticipating scale from day one. By utilizing Cloudflare Workers and Queues, developers can build a robust ingestion layer that handles traffic spikes gracefully and processes data securely. Open-source projects like Codra provide excellent blueprints for implementing these patterns in real-world scenarios.

#9633. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

The global cybersecurity community will gather in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from December 1–3, 2026, as Black Hat Middle East and Africa (Black Hat MEA) returns for another edition of one of the region's major cybersecurity events. Bringing together security professionals, ethical hackers, technology companies, enterprise leaders, and innovators, the three-day event will offer a platform to explore emerging threats, exchange expertise, and discuss the technologies shaping the future of information security.

Taking place at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center in Malham, Black Hat MEA 2026 will bring together different parts of the cybersecurity ecosystem through conferences, specialized training, competitions, exhibitions, and investment-focused programming. The event is designed to connect the international cybersecurity community with regional organizations and businesses working to strengthen digital infrastructure and security capabilities.

Since its launch in Riyadh in 2021, Black Hat MEA has developed into a major business-to-business platform for the cybersecurity industry in the Middle East and Africa. Its focus spans information security, ethical hacking, cyber defense, enterprise resilience, and security innovation.

The 2026 edition will bring together cybersecurity practitioners, researchers, enterprise decision-makers, technology vendors, investors, and security enthusiasts. Attendees will have opportunities to learn from industry experts, discover new solutions, participate in hands-on activities, and build relationships with professionals working across the global information security landscape.

Black Hat MEA 2026 will feature a diverse program covering several areas of cybersecurity and technology. The conference program will provide a platform for industry experts and practitioners to share insights, discuss security developments, and explore the challenges facing organizations today. These discussions will offer attendees perspectives on the changing cybersecurity landscape and the approaches being developed to address evolving threats.

The event will also feature specialized cybersecurity training, giving participants opportunities to develop practical skills and deepen their technical knowledge. Hands-on learning remains an important part of the cybersecurity ecosystem, particularly for professionals working in penetration testing, ethical hacking, threat detection, and defensive security.

Competitions will bring another dimension to the event, creating opportunities for participants to test their technical capabilities and engage with the wider cybersecurity community. Meanwhile, the exhibition floor will showcase cybersecurity products, services, and technologies from companies working across the information security industry. Black Hat MEA will also include investment-focused programming, creating opportunities for businesses, startups, investors, and technology leaders to connect and explore potential collaborations.

Together, these activities position the event as more than a traditional industry conference. It offers a space for technical learning, business development, networking, and discussions around the future of cybersecurity.

HackerNoon is partnering with Black Hat MEA 2026 as an Official Media Partner, supporting the event's reach and visibility across the global technology community. As an independent technology publication platform, HackerNoon connects millions of readers with stories, insights, and developments from across the technology industry. Its community includes technology professionals, founders, developers, entrepreneurs, researchers, and businesses working across emerging technology sectors.

Through this media partnership, HackerNoon looks forward to amplifying conversations around cybersecurity, information security, ethical hacking, and security innovation while bringing greater visibility to the people and organizations contributing to the industry.

Black Hat MEA 2026 will take place from December 1–3, 2026, at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center, Malham, Saudi Arabia.

Organized by Tahaluf and co-organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP), the event continues to bring international cybersecurity expertise and regional technology ambitions together in Riyadh.

For cybersecurity professionals looking to expand their knowledge, businesses exploring security solutions, or technology leaders interested in connecting with the global information security community, Black Hat MEA 2026 offers three days of opportunities to learn, collaborate, and explore what's next for cybersecurity.

#9630. 규제 샌드박스 대 전면 금지: 암호화폐 거버넌스를 둘러싼 글로벌 이분법적 접근

블록체인 기술과 암호화폐의 출현은 전 세계 기존 금융 시스템과 규제 프레임워크에 지대한 도전 과제를 던져줬다.

탈중앙화되고 투명하며 검열 저항적인 금융 인프라를 향한 열망에서 탄생한 이 혁신들은 빠르게 진화하며 새로운 자산군, 결제 시스템, 그리고 비즈니스 모델을 창출했다. 하지만 이들의 국경 없는 특성, 급속한 발전 속도, 그리고 내재된 변동성은 금융 안정성, 소비자 보호, 자금세탁 방지(AML), 테러 자금 조달 방지(CTF), 그리고 시스템적 위험에 대한 심각한 우려를 불러일으켰다.

이러한 다면적인 현상에 대응하여 전 세계 각국은 극명하게 다른 접근 방식을 채택했다. 본질적으로 두 가지 주요 철학으로 나뉘는데, 바로 '규제 샌드박스'를 통한 통제된 실험으로 혁신을 수용하는 방식과 '전면 금지'라는 엄격한 조치를 택하는 방식이다.

이러한 차이는 단순히 규제 선호도의 문제가 아니라, 깊이 뿌리내린 국가 경제 전략, 기술 철학, 그리고 지정학적 고려 사항을 반영한다. 이 글에서는 이 두 가지 대조적인 규제 패러다임을 깊이 탐구하며, 그 배경이 되는 동기, 기술적 메커니즘, 실제 구현 사례, 내재된 한계, 그리고 금융 및 기술의 미래에 대한 광범위한 함의를 분석한다.

다양한 관할권이 선택한 길을 고찰함으로써, 복잡한 디지털 자산 환경을 헤쳐나가는 각 접근 방식의 효율성과 지속 가능성에 대한 전문가적 관점을 제시하고자 한다.

2009년 글로벌 금융 위기 이후 비트코인이 탄생하며 중앙 기관 없이 운영되는 P2P 전자 현금 시스템이라는 혁명적인 개념이 세상에 나왔다.

이 근본적인 혁신은 수천 개의 다른 암호화폐와 블록체인 기반 애플리케이션, 즉 Web3의 발전을 촉발했다. 초기에는 정부와 금융 규제 당국이 이러한 신생 기술을 분류하고 이해하는 데 어려움을 겪었고, 이는 상당한 규제 공백기로 이어졌다.

암호화폐 시장이 규모와 복잡성 면에서 성장하고 소매 및 기관 투자자 모두의 관심을 끌면서 명확한 규제 프레임워크의 필요성은 점점 더 시급해졌다. 몇 가지 주요 동인이 규제 개입을 촉발했다.

첫째, 금융 안정성이다. 변동성이 큰 암호화폐 자산이 전통 금융 시장과 얽히거나 스테이블코인이 적절한 준비금을 갖추지 못할 경우 시스템적 위험이 발생할 수 있다는 우려가 제기됐다.

둘째, 소비자 및 투자자 보호 문제다. 사기, 시장 조작, 불투명한 자금 조달 메커니즘(예: ICO), 그리고 탈중앙화 시스템에서 투자자 구제 수단의 부족은 중요한 안전장치의 필요성을 부각했다.

셋째, 자금세탁 방지(AML) 및 테러 자금 조달 방지(CTF)다. 초기 암호화폐 거래의 인지된 익명성은 불법 금융에 대한 경고등을 켰고, FATF와 같은 국제 기구들이 지침을 발표하도록 만들었다.

넷째, 과세 문제다. 정부는 암호화폐 관련 수익과 거래를 추적하고 과세하는 데 어려움을 겪었으며, 이는 잠재적인 세수 손실로 이어졌다.

마지막으로, 통화 주권 및 자본 통제에 대한 우려다. 일부 국가에서는 탈중앙화된 통화의 등장이 국내 통화 정책을 통제하고 국경을 넘는 자본 흐름을 관리하는 능력에 위협이 될 수 있다고 봤다.

이러한 동인들은 두 가지 지배적인 규제 철학으로 합쳐졌다. 하나는 기술적으로 진보적이거나 글로벌 금융 허브를 목표로 하는 경제권에서 자주 채택됐는데, 기술을 책임감 있게 이해하고 통합하려 했다.

이는 규제 샌드박스의 개발로 이어졌다. 다른 하나는 중앙 통제, 어떤 대가를 치르더라도 금융 안정성 확보, 또는 규제 역량 부족에 강하게 초점을 맞추어 위험을 극복할 수 없다고 보고 전면적인 금지를 택했다.

규제 접근 방식의 차이는 암호화폐가 제시하는 위험과 기회에 대한 근본적으로 다른 평가를 반영한다.

규제 샌드박스는 금융 규제 당국이 설정한 통제된 테스트 환경으로, 기업들이 완화되거나 수정된 규제 프레임워크 아래에서 제한된 기간 동안 실제 시장 환경에서 새로운 제품, 서비스 또는 비즈니스 모델을 시험할 수 있도록 허용한다. 주된 목표는 혁신을 촉진하는 동시에 소비자 보호와 금융 안정성을 보장하는 것이다.

주요 특징을 살펴보자. 참여 기업은 특정 규제 요건의 면제 또는 수정을 통해 기존 규제의 모든 준수 비용을 부담하지 않고도 실험할 수 있어 규제 부담이 줄어든다.

규제 당국은 샌드박스 참여 기업과 긴밀히 협력하며 지침을 제공하고 활동을 모니터링하며 혁신의 성과와 위험에 대한 데이터를 수집한다. 이를 통해 규제 당국은 신흥 기술을 직접 학습한다.

각 샌드박스 진입은 명확한 목표, 제한된 운영 범위(예: 고객 수, 거래량), 그리고 명시된 기간을 갖는 명확한 테스트 매개변수를 가진다. 완화된 규칙에도 불구하고 공개 요구 사항, 보상 제도 또는 노출 제한과 같은 소비자 보호를 위한 명시적인 조치가 마련되어 소비자 보호가 이루어진다.

테스트 단계가 완료되면 기업은 기존 규제에 따라 완전한 인가를 받거나, 새로운 맞춤형 라이선스를 받거나, 제품이 실행 불가능하거나 너무 위험하다고 판단될 경우 운영을 중단하는 종료 전략을 갖는다.

장점은 규제 샌드박스가 새로운 기술에 대한 초기 진입 장벽을 낮춤으로써 혁신을 촉진하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 점이다. 이를 통해 규제 당국은 복잡한 디지털 자산과 블록체인 애플리케이션에 대한 더 깊은 이해를 얻고, 시대에 뒤떨어진 규칙을 적용하는 대신 목적에 맞는 규제를 개발하는 데 정보를 제공한다.

이러한 접근 방식은 인재와 자본을 유치하여 관할권을 금융 기술 분야의 리더로 자리매김하게 한다. 또한, 규제 프레임워크를 업계와 함께 반복적으로 학습하고 공동으로 만들어 나갈 수 있도록 돕는다.

단점으로는 샌드박스가 규제 당국에 많은 자원을 요구하며 전문 지식이 필요하다는 점이다. 제한된 범위는 특히 고도로 상호 연결된 탈중앙화 금융(DeFi) 프로토콜의 경우 시스템적 위험을 완전히 포착하지 못할 수도 있다. 또한, 성공적인 샌드박스 프로젝트를 완전한 규제 준수로 확장하는 것이 느리고 복잡할 수 있다는 과제도 있다.

전면 금지는 특정 암호화폐 관련 활동에 대한 포괄적인 금지를 의미한다. 이는 거래, 채굴, ICO 금지부터 암호화폐를 교환 매체로 사용하는 것을 제한하거나 심지어 단순히 소유하는 것까지 금지하는 것을 포함한다.

주요 특징은 금지가 일반적으로 불이행에 대한 엄격한 처벌을 동반하여 금지된 활동에 대한 참여를 억제하는 것을 목표로 한다는 점이다. 이는 명확하고 엄격한 집행을 의미한다.

이러한 접근 방식은 종종 금융 시스템, 자본 흐름 및 통화 정책에 대한 중앙화된 통제를 유지하려는 강한 열망에 의해 주도된다. 주된 동기는 복잡한 규제 개발에 참여하지 않고도 인지된 위험을 완전히 그리고 즉시 제거하려는 위험 제거(인지된)다.

장점을 보면, 규제 관점에서 볼 때 금지는 인지된 위협의 즉각적인 중단을 제공하며, 복잡하고 빠르게 진화하는 기술과 씨름할 필요성을 제거함으로써 규제 환경을 단순화한다. 이론적으로는 자본 유출을 방지하고 통화 주권을 유지하며 시장 변동성 및 불법 금융과 관련된 위험을 완화할 수 있다.

단점 중 가장 중요한 것은 탈중앙화되고 국경 없는 기술에 대한 내재된 비효율성이다. 활동은 종종 지하, 해외 또는 P2P 네트워크로 이동하여 집행을 어렵게 만들고 불법 활동을 덜 투명한 채널로 몰아넣을 수 있다.

금지는 국내 혁신을 억압하여 인재와 자본이 더 관대한 관할권으로 "두뇌 유출"을 초래한다. 또한 디지털 자산 공간과 관련된 일자리 창출, 새로운 산업, 세수와 같은 잠재적인 경제적 이점을 포기하게 된다.

더 나아가, 금지는 종종 기술에 정통한 인구를 소외시키고 기술 발전을 저해하는 권위주의적 조치로 비칠 수 있다.

이러한 상이한 접근 방식의 근본 원인은 종종 한 국가의 경제 구조, 정치 시스템 및 위험 감수 성향과 연결된다. 확고한 금융 서비스 부문과 글로벌 경쟁력에 대한 열망을 가진 국가들은 혁신을 성장의 필수 동력으로 보며 샌드박스 쪽으로 기울어지는 경향이 있다.

반대로 엄격한 자본 통제, 보다 권위주의적인 거버넌스 스타일, 또는 장기적인 혁신보다 즉각적인 안정을 우선시하는 국가들은 전면적인 금지를 부과하는 경향이 더 크다.

영국(금융감독청 - FCA)은 2016년 핀테크 규제 샌드박스를 설립하며 선구적인 역할을 했고, 여기에는 블록체인 및 분산원장기술(DLT) 프로젝트가 명시적으로 포함됐다. FCA는 다수의 기수를 유치하여 기업들이 토큰화된 증권 플랫폼, 블록체인 기반 송금, 스테이블코인 모델과 같은 혁신적인 솔루션을 테스트할 수 있도록 했다.

예를 들어, DLT를 활용한 채무 상품 발행 및 결제 프로젝트가 테스트되어, FCA에 디지털 증권 샌드박스와 광범위한 스테이블코인 규제와 같은 현재 진행 중인 정책 논의에 필수적인 통찰력을 제공했다.

싱가포르(싱가포르 통화청 - MAS)는 지속적으로 자신을 글로벌 핀테크 허브로 포지셔닝해 왔다. 2016년에 출시된 핀테크 규제 샌드박스는 유연성과 반응성으로 높이 평가받는다. MAS는 샌드박스를 활용하여 은행 간 결제 및 정산에 DLT 사용을 탐색한 프로젝트 우빈(Project Ubin)과 같은 프로젝트를 촉진했다.

이후 제정된 지불 서비스법(Payment Services Act, PSA)은 광범위한 암호화폐 서비스 제공업체를 특별히 규제하며, 샌드박스 실험을 통해 얻은 통찰력과 디지털 자산을 금융 생태계에 통합하려는 적극적인 입장을 반영한다.

종종 "크립토 밸리"라고 불리는 스위스(금융시장감독청 - FINMA)는 블록체인 혁신에 매우 우호적인 환경을 조성했다. FINMA는 2019년 DLT 기반 비즈니스 모델을 위해 특별히 설계된 핀테크 라이선스를 도입하여 공공 예금을 받지 않는 기업에 대해 더 가벼운 규제 요건을 제공했다.

이러한 접근 방식은 Sygnum Bank 및 SEBA Bank와 같은 규제된 블록체인 은행의 인가를 촉진했으며, 이들 은행은 디지털 자산에 대한 기관급 커스터디 및 거래 서비스를 제공하여 혁신에서 완전한 규제 승인으로 가는 명확한 경로를 보여준다.

중국은 암호화폐 활동에 대한 포괄적인 금지를 시행한 가장 대표적인 국가다. 2017년 인민은행(PBOC)은 ICO를 금지했고, 이어서 암호화폐 거래소에 대한 단속을 실시했다. 2021년에는 모든 암호화폐 거래 및 채굴 활동을 불법 금융 활동으로 선언하며 금지 조치를 대폭 확대했다.

이러한 결정은 금융 안정성, 자본 유출, (채굴의) 환경 영향, 그리고 사회 및 경제적 통제를 유지하려는 열망, 특히 중앙은행 디지털 통화(CBDC)인 디지털 위안화 추진을 배경으로 했다. 이는 암호화폐 채굴자와 거래소의 대규모 중국 이탈을 초래했다.

이집트와 카타르는 종종 종교적 해석(샤리아 법)과 국가 안보 우려를 인용하며 엄격한 금지를 시행했다. 이집트에서는 중앙은행(CBE)이 2018년 암호화폐 거래 및 발행을 금지했고, 2020년에는 이러한 입장을 더욱 강화했다.

마찬가지로 카타르의 금융 규제 기관인 카타르 금융센터 규제 당국(QFCRA)은 2020년 가상 자산 서비스에 대한 금지를 발표하여 QFC 내에서 암호화폐 자산과 관련된 모든 활동을 금지했다. 이러한 금지는 금융 혁신에 대한 보수적인 접근 방식을 반영하며, 인지된 안정성과 전통적 가치를 우선시한다.

인도(과거 사례, 현재 규제 중)는 완전한 전면 금지를 유지하지는 않았지만, 그 규제 여정은 금지에 대한 강한 유혹을 보여준다. 2018년 인도 중앙은행(RBI)은 규제 대상 기관이 암호화폐를 취급하는 것을 금지하는 회람을 발행하여 사실상 은행 금지를 부과했다.

비록 이 조치가 2020년 대법원에 의해 나중에 뒤집혔지만, 정부는 "사설 암호화폐"를 금지하는 법안을 도입하는 것을 반복적으로 검토했다. 이러한 오락가락하는 입장은 금융 안정성, 자본 통제, 불법 금융에 대한 인도 정부 내의 뿌리 깊은 우려를 강조하며, 결국 디지털 자산에 대한 높은 과세 및 규제 프레임워크로 정착하게 됐다.

두 가지 규제 접근 방식은 그 대조적인 철학에도 불구하고 각자의 한계와 과제를 안고 있다.

가장 중요한 과제 중 하나는 통제된 샌드박스 환경에서 완전한 규제 준수로의 전환이다. 새롭고 맞춤화된 규제를 개발하는 것은 느릴 수 있으며, 성공적인 샌드박스 프로젝트의 향후 경로는 항상 명확하지 않아 실험 후 규제 불확실성을 야기할 수 있다.

전 세계적으로 여러 샌드박스가 존재하며, 각각 약간 다른 매개변수와 엄격성 수준을 가지고 있어 기업들이 가장 강력하게 규제된 환경이 아닌 가장 관대한 환경을 찾는 "샌드박스 쇼핑"으로 이어질 수 있다. 이는 전반적인 글로벌 금융 시스템의 무결성을 훼손할 수 있다.

샌드박스를 운영하는 것은 규제 당국에게 상당한 인적 및 기술적 자원을 요구한다. 복잡한 DLT 아키텍처를 이해하고 새로운 위험을 평가하며 맞춤형 지침을 제공할 수 있는 고도로 숙련된 인력이 필요한데, 많은 규제 기관이 이러한 인력을 갖추지 못할 수 있다.

중앙 집중식 핀테크 혁신에는 효과적이지만, 샌드박스는 진정으로 탈중앙화된 프로토콜(예: DeFi)의 고유한 과제를 적절하게 다루는 데 어려움을 겪을 수 있다. 이러한 프로토콜에는 통제된 환경에서 규제하거나 협력할 수 있는 식별 가능한 중앙 주체가 없기 때문이다.

정밀하게 관리되지 않으면, 통제된 환경조차도 성공적인 샌드박스 프로젝트가 적절한 감독 없이 빠르게 확장되거나 예상치 못한 방식으로 전통 금융 시스템과 상호 운용될 경우 시스템적 위험에 의도치 않게 기여할 수 있다.

블록체인 기술의 탈중앙화되고 국경 없는 특성은 완전한 금지를 효과적으로 집행하는 것을 극도로 어렵게, 심지어 불가능하게 만든다. 암호화폐 활동은 종종 P2P 네트워크, 해외 거래소 또는 VPN으로 보호되는 플랫폼으로 이동하여 모니터링하기가 더 어려워진다.

암호화폐를 금지하는 것은 빠르게 성장하는 기술 분야에서 국내 혁신의 잠재력을 포기하는 것을 의미한다. 이는 기업가와 개발자들이 암호화폐에 더 우호적인 관할권으로 이동하게 만들고, 잠재적인 경제 성장, 일자리 창출, 세수 손실로 이어진다.

암호화폐 활동을 지하로 몰아넣음으로써, 금지는 의도치 않게 투명성을 감소시킨다. 이는 법 집행 기관이 불법 거래를 추적하는 것을 상당히 어렵게 만들어, 금지가 종종 달성하려는 AML/CTF 목표 자체를 효과적으로 훼손한다.

금지는 규제 당국이 기술에 대한 직접적인 지식과 이해를 얻는 것을 방해하여, 궁극적으로 기술의 글로벌 확산에 대처할 준비가 부족하게 만들고 미래 기술 변화에 뒤처질 수 있다.

엄격한 금지는 개인과 기관이 디지털 자산을 보존하거나 글로벌 암호화폐 시장에 참여하려고 함에 따라 자본 유출로 이어질 수 있다. 또한, 이러한 금지를 퇴행적인 조치로 보는 젊고 기술에 정통한 인구층을 소외시킬 수도 있다.

암호화폐 규제에 대한 글로벌한 차이, 즉 규제 샌드박스의 신중한 실험과 전면 금지라는 무딘 도구 사이의 대립은 혁신 촉진과 인지된 위험 완화 사이의 근본적인 긴장을 반영한다. 전면적인 금지는 즉각적이고 피상적인 통제감을 제공하지만, 장기적인 효율성과 지속 가능성은 매우 의문스럽다.

블록체인 기술의 탈중앙화되고 국경 없는, 그리고 검열 저항적인 특성은 본질적으로 완전한 근절을 불가능하게 한다. 역사는 기술 발전을 금지하려는 시도가 종종 이를 지하로 몰아넣어 덜 투명하고 모니터링하기 어려운 생태계를 만들었음을 보여줬다.

이는 결국 제거하려 했던 바로 그 위험을 악화시키는 동시에 막대한 경제적, 혁신적 잠재력을 희생시킨다.

반면, 규제 샌드박스는 내재된 복잡성과 자원 요구에도 불구하고 보다 실용적이고 미래 지향적인 접근 방식을 대표한다. 이들은 디지털 자산의 변혁적 잠재력을 인정하면서도, 규제 당국이 학습하고 적응하며 목적에 맞는 규제를 공동으로 만들 수 있는 구조화된 프레임워크를 제공한다.

이러한 반복적인 학습 과정은 관할권이 강력한 소비자 보호, 금융 안정성, 그리고 AML/CTF 준수와 혁신의 균형을 맞추는 미묘한 정책을 개발할 수 있도록 한다. 영국, 싱가포르, 스위스와 같은 국가들은 적극적인 참여를 통해 디지털 자산 혁명의 선두에 서서 인재와 자본을 유치해 왔다.

궁극적으로 한 국가가 선택하는 길은 그 국가의 광범위한 경제 철학, 적응형 거버넌스 역량, 그리고 기술적 혼란을 수용하거나 저항하려는 의지를 반영한다. 전문가적 관점에서 볼 때, 전면 금지의 즉각적인 매력이 절대적인 통제를 추구하는 이들에게는 매력적일지 모르지만, 장기적으로는 대체로 자멸적인 전략이다.

글로벌 금융의 미래는 필연적으로 블록체인 기술과 얽히게 될 것이다. 따라서 국가들에게 더 지속 가능하고 유익한 접근 방식은 이러한 혁신을 헛되이 금지하려 하기보다는 지능적으로 통합하고 규제하는 것이다. 규제 차익 거래를 방지하고 안전하고 효율적이며 혁신적인 글로벌 디지털 자산 생태계를 조성하기 위해서는 국제 협력과 조화된 규제 표준이 필수적이다.

※ 본 칼럼은 정보 제공을 목적으로 하며, 투자 권유가 아닙니다. 모든 투자 결정은 본인의 판단과 책임 하에 이루어져야 합니다.

#9629. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

#9628. A 7-point checklist before you let Codex review Claude Code commits

Claude Code writes, Codex reviews, a gate decides what merges. Here's the short version I check before trusting that loop on a repo. The full walkthrough, with the prompts, is in How to make Codex review Claude Code's commits.

1. Codex runs read-only. codex exec -s read-only --color never --output-last-message -, with the prompt on stdin. The reviewer can read files and run git diff, but it can't write or hand back a patch.

2. One verdict line, saved under the commit hash. Verdict: ACCEPT or Verdict: CHANGES REQUIRED, read only from the --output-last-message file. A crash, an empty answer or two Verdict lines leave no saved verdict, so the commit can't merge.

3. A brief exists before the code. Every line under "Done means" is something a reviewer can confirm from the diff or a test. Write "a customer email with a comma is escaped", never "export works well".

4. Each new test failed on the base commit. The engine that writes the code often writes the tests too. A test that already passes on the old code proves nothing about the change.

5. House rules live where both engines read them. CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex. Keep the AGENTS.md part short: Codex stops adding instruction files once their combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default.

6. The reviewer answers every line. Met with a file:line, not met with what's missing, or not checkable with the evidence it would need. Findings outside the brief need a concrete failure. Style preferences aren't findings.

7. Rounds have a hard cap. Later rounds raise only what blocks the merge. If the last allowed round says CHANGES REQUIRED, the merge stays blocked and a person decides.

The merge is refused unless that exact commit has a test pass and a saved ACCEPT. A test pass alone won't catch a test Claude Code weakened in the same commit, so that falls to the reviewer: what my review gate does with weakened and deleted tests.

If you want the whole setup prebuilt, the Two Engines Kit for Claude Code and Codex is a paid kit I made, built on information gathered since the first Codex and Claude CLIs.

#9627. क्या YouTube के ऑटो-जनरेटेड कैप्शन इतने सही हैं कि उन्हें कोट किया जा सके?

ज़्यादातर YouTube वीडियो में ट्रांसक्रिप्ट होती है, और उनमें से अधिकतर को स्पीच रिकग्निशन ने लिखा होता है। वीडियो के साथ चलने के लिए यह ठीक है। लेकिन किसी पेपर, न्यूज़ स्टोरी या क़ानूनी नोट में कोट देने के लिए सवाल यह है कि ऑटोमैटिक टेक्स्ट असल में कही गई बात से कितना दूर है, और उसके टाइमस्टैम्प सही सेकंड पर इशारा करते हैं या नहीं। जिस वीडियो में दोनों तरह के कैप्शन हों, वह इसका सीधा जवाब देता है।

वीडियो NASA का अपलोड किया हुआ राष्ट्रपति कैनेडी का 1962 का राइस यूनिवर्सिटी वाला भाषण है (WZyRbnpGyzQ, 18 मिनट)। इसमें दो अंग्रेज़ी ट्रैक हैं: एक किसी इंसान का लिखा हुआ और एक YouTube का बनाया हुआ। दोनों को Python पैकेज youtube-transcript-api से लिस्ट और डाउनलोड किया जा सकता है:

हर एंट्री टेक्स्ट की एक लाइन होती है, जिसके साथ स्टार्ट टाइम और सेकंड में अवधि होती है।

शब्द-दर-शब्द तुलना करने पर (लोअरकेस, विराम चिह्न हटाकर, Python के difflib.SequenceMatcher से अलाइन करके) दोनों ट्रैक भाषण के लगभग 95% हिस्से पर एक जैसे हैं:

छह प्रतिशत छोटा लगता है, जब तक यह न देखें कि वे कौन से शब्द हैं। स्पीच रिकग्निशन आम शब्दों पर अच्छा करता है और नामों, संख्याओं और तकनीकी शब्दों पर बुरा, और कोट अक्सर इन्हीं हिस्सों पर टिका होता है:

एक खाली जगह भी है। लगभग 4:47 पर ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक "both must be" से सीधे "determined and cannot be deterred" पर कूद जाता है। बीच के 28 शब्द, "enterprised and overcome with answerable courage. If this capsule history of our progress teaches us anything, it is that man, in his quest for knowledge and progress, is", उसमें हैं ही नहीं। ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक में कुछ भी इस खाली जगह को चिह्नित नहीं करता।

इस भाषण की जो लाइन लोग कोट करते हैं, वह 9:18 पर है। इंसानी ट्रैक में यह एक लाइन है, विराम चिह्नों के साथ और एक स्टार्ट टाइम के साथ:

ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक में यह तीन ओवरलैप होती लाइनों में फैली है, और पहला शब्द पिछली लाइन का है:

ऑटोमैटिक कैप्शन रोलिंग डिस्प्ले के लिए बने होते हैं, एक बार में कुछ शब्द, इसलिए उनकी लाइनें वाक्यों की जगह बोलने के टाइमिंग का पीछा करती हैं। कोट करने के लिए इससे दो बातें निकलती हैं। 9:18 वाली लाइन कॉपी करने पर ऐसा टुकड़ा मिलता है जो वाक्य के बीच से शुरू होता है, और "not" वाली लाइन का स्टार्ट टाइम 9:15 है, यानी कोट से तीन सेकंड पहले। कैप्शन के तौर पर दोनों में कुछ ग़लत नहीं; सायटेशन के तौर पर दोनों ग़लत हैं।

इस मामले में व्याकरण बचा रहा, "they are", उस वर्शन के उलट जो ज़्यादातर लोगों को याद है ("because it is hard")। लेकिन कुछ लाइनों बाद "we are willing" बन गया "we're willing", और ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक से लिया गया कोट कैनेडी के मुँह में ऐसा संक्षिप्त रूप डाल देगा जो उन्होंने कहा ही नहीं।

osFoundry डेस्कटॉप ऐप का ट्रांसक्रिप्ट टूल, जो उसी कंप्यूटर से कैप्शन लाता है जिस पर वह चल रहा है, यह चुनाव Rust की कुछ लाइनों में करता है। YouTube ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक को kind: "asr" से चिह्नित करता है, और ऐप पहले इंसान का लिखा अंग्रेज़ी ट्रैक लेता है, फिर कोई भी अंग्रेज़ी ट्रैक, फिर कोई भी इंसानी ट्रैक, और फिर जो भी मौजूद हो:

जब कोई लाइन रेफ़रेंस के रूप में सेव होती है, तो उसका स्टार्ट टाइम लिंक का t पैरामीटर बन जाता है। समय नीचे की ओर राउंड किया जाता है, ताकि वीडियो शब्दों से सेकंड के एक हिस्से पहले शुरू हो, पहले शब्द के बाद नहीं:

9:18 वाली लाइन के लिए यह &t=558s है, उस लाइन के लिए जो 558.9 सेकंड पर शुरू होती है।

बहुत से वीडियो में सिर्फ़ ऑटोमैटिक ट्रैक होता है। तब वह सर्च इंडेक्स है, स्रोत नहीं: उससे मोटे तौर पर पता करें कि बात कहाँ कही गई, वह हिस्सा चलाएँ और कोट ऑडियो सुनकर लिखें। नाम और संख्याएँ किसी दूसरे स्रोत से जाँचें, और ऐसे हिस्सों की उम्मीद रखें जो बिना किसी निशान के ग़ायब हैं। सेकंड तक पहुँचने वाला लिंक फिर भी रखने लायक़ है, क्योंकि उससे पाठक वही जाँच कुछ सेकंड में दोहरा सकता है।

यहाँ इस्तेमाल हुआ डेस्कटॉप ऐप osFoundry डाउनलोड पेज से मुफ़्त है।

#9624. 3 Personality Traits Associated With Infidelity

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner.

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner.

People who are low on conscientiousness are more likely to cheat on their partner, research finds.

People who are not conscientious are careless, badly organised and find it hard to resist temptation.

People who are more extraverted are also more likely to cheat on their partner, the researchers found.

It is probably because extraverted people have a wider social circle and so more opportunities to cheat.

Also, extraverts are impulsive, sensation-seekers who can easily succumb to their desires.

The conclusions come from a survey of 208 people, who were asked about their relationships and whether they had cheated.

Up to 50% of people admit cheating on their partner, the authors write:

“Early studies reported that by the age of 40, 50% of all married men and more than 25% of all married women have engaged in extramarital sexual behavior.

Three decades later, an estimated 50% of men continued to engage in sexual and/or emotional extramarital relations while 40% of women engaged in similar relationships.”

The results of the study revealed that cheaters tend to be low in conscientiousness, extraverted and open to experience.

Extraverts tend to seek out stimulation, the authors write:

“Extroverts may be inclined to cheat to obtain stimulation and prevent boredom.

Extroversion may also facilitate less investment in the relationship when those with this trait seek out others for stimulation, thereby decreasing commitment and resulting in cheating behaviours.”

The third personality trait associated with infidelity is openness to experience.

Openness to experience is linked to intellect and creativity.

“…cheaters may perceive themselves as having stronger intellect and stronger creativity compared to that of their partners, leading them to seek out partners that may be a better, that is, similar, match.”

The study was published in the journal Current Psychology (Orzeck & Lung, 2005).

Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean

The most recent trial confirms that two nutrients can reduce deaths from heart attacks and cancer.

Omega-3 fatty acids from fish oil can significantly reduce heart attacks and vitamin D supplementation can significantly lower the number of deaths caused by different types of cancer.

Researchers studied 26,000 American adults in the VITAL clinical trial for five years to see if fish oil or vitamin D would definitely ward off cardiovascular disease or cancer.

The outcomes were reassuring: marine omega-3 fatty acid intake was linked to a significant drop in heart attacks.

One-and-half servings per week of dietary fish intake showed the maximum heart health benefits, but higher dietary fish intake didn’t help more.

The greatest decrease in heart attacks was seen in African-Americans.

The benefit of 1 gram of omega-3 fish oil supplementation showed a small decrease in major cardiovascular events like stroke and death from cardiovascular disease.

Vitamin D3 or cholecalciferol intake at a dose of 2000 IU per day showed a significant decrease of death from cancer for those who took it for at least two years.

However, supplementation with vitamin D3 capsules didn’t significantly lower incidence of any type of cancer or cardiovascular disease.

Dr. JoAnn Manson, the study’s first author, said:

“The pattern of findings suggests a complex balance of benefits and risks for each intervention and points to the need for additional research to determine which individuals may be most likely to derive a net benefit from these supplements.”

Dr. Stephanie Faubion, NAMS medical director, said:

“With heart disease and cancer representing the most significant health threats to women, it is imperative that we continue to study the viability of options that prevent these diseases and help women survive them.”

The 1 gram omega-3 fish oil supplementation used in the VITAL clinical trial was Omacor, a prescription medicine for adults.

The capsule contains 840 milligrams marine omega-3 fatty acids, of which 465 mg is eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and 375 mg is docosahexaenoic acid (DHA).

The study was presented at the North American Menopause Society (NAMS) Annual Meeting in Chicago (Manson et al., 2019).

#9618. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

#9614. This Vitamin Reduces Mental Health Problems By 50%

Around half the world’s population are thought to have an insufficiency of this vitamin.

Around half the world’s population are thought to have an insufficiency of this vitamin.

A triple dose of vitamin D3 supplementation in the first two years of life reduces the chance of mental health problems later on by around 50 percent, a high-quality experiment finds.

Infants who were given 30 µg of vitamin D daily, which is three times the recommended dose, were only half as likely to have internalising problems by age 6-8.

Internalising problems are those in which a person keeps their problems to themselves, including depression, anxiety, loneliness and withdrawal.

Dr Samuel Sandboge, the study’s first author, said:

“Our results suggest that a higher dose of vitamin D3 supplementation during the first years of life may reduce the risk of internalizing psychiatric symptoms in late preschool and early school age.”

The randomised controlled trial, which was carried out in Finland, was inspired by the link found between low childhood vitamin D levels and mental health problems.

Almost 350 children were given either a dose of 10 µg or 30 µg of vitamin D from age 2 weeks until 2-years-old.

The results showed that at 6- to 8-years-old, almost 12 percent of children given 10 µg had significant internalising problems.

In the 30 µg group, though, this figure was under 6 percent.

No differences were seen in the number of externalising problems.

Externalising disorders include ADHD and conduct disorder.

Later in life externalising disorders include substance abuse, antisocial personality disorders and even psychopathy.

Dr Samuel Sandboge warned that the study has drawbacks:

“The results and their potential implications are interesting, but further research is needed to confirm the results.

In the interpretation of the results, we must note, among other things, that we studied the psychiatric symptoms only as parent-reported.

Furthermore, the participants of the study were children with Nordic ancestry living in Finland who had good levels of vitamin D.”

Around half the world’s population are thought to have an insufficiency of vitamin D, and 10 percent are deficient.

Vitamin D plays an important role in the development of the brain.

It is notable that a rise in autism and ADHD rates has happened at a time when there have been significant drops in average levels of vitamin D.

The study was published in JAMA Network Open (Sandboge et al., 2023).

#9603. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.
